data.description:
## 1. Technical Environment
* Plugin Version: dso v1.17.11
* code_version: df8313c8ab4e025bafbe156577ca2ae69b095605
* Discovered during: SC10 evidence sprint (story c4f1-c18d-0000-4001, epic b575-ac1c-f720-4839) — multi-cycle arbiter dispatch on PR #270 after bug 230d was fixed
* Related: bug 230d-6cab (cycle ledger reconstruction endpoint, fixed in PR #268). This bug surfaces ONLY after 230d is fixed and a live PR drives 4 cycles.

## 2. Incident Overview

### Expected Behavior

`dispatch_arbiter` in `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/arbiter.py:257` should dispatch the `code-reviewer-arbiter` opus agent and receive a JSON array of per-finding rulings — one entry per unresolved finding — each with `ruling ∈ {BLOCK, DEFER, DROP}`, `rationale`, `severity`, `impact_class`, `cross_reviewer_agreement`, `cross_cycle_pattern`. This matches the agent contract in `code-reviewer-arbiter.md` and epic b575 SC1.

### Actual Behavior

On PR #270 (commit_sha=0656f88f90de34f505c122bc48518d2d021f03e9) at cycle 4 (max_cycles=4) with 12 unresolved findings, the arbiter agent returned exactly **1 ruling** instead of 12. The runner's length-mismatch detection at `arbiter.py:375-396` fired `arbiter_length_mismatch findings=12 rulings=1` to stderr and fell back to the safety path — emitting a BLOCK ruling for every critical/important finding with rationale `"Arbiter response length mismatch (got 1 rulings for 12 findings); defaulting to BLOCK; manual review required."` All 9 critical/important findings received BLOCK; minor findings received no ruling. **DEFER and DROP rulings are unreachable** from this code path until the agent's array-length contract is respected.

### Empirical evidence (PR #270, cycle 4)

DSO-Arbiter-Ruling comment posted at https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/270 with body:

```
DSO-Arbiter-Ruling: 4 commit_sha=0656f88f90de34f505c122bc48518d2d021f03e9

### Arbiter Rulings

[
  {"ruling": "BLOCK", "rationale": "Arbiter response length mismatch ...", "finding_index": 0, "severity": "critical", ...},
  {"ruling": "BLOCK", "rationale": "Arbiter response length mismatch ...", "finding_index": 1, "severity": "critical", ...},
  ... (9 entries total, all BLOCK fallback) ...
]
```

CI run 26273145856 attempt 4, llm-review job 77340543945. Job log:
```
INFO: cycle 4 — relation distribution: {'new_introduced_justified': 0, 'new_introduced_unjustified': 12, ...}
WARNING: DSO_REVIEW_CYCLE=3 disagrees with ledger cycle_num=4; ledger wins (authoritative)
arbiter_length_mismatch findings=12 rulings=1
```

The cycle counter advanced 1→4 correctly (proves bug 230d fix is working). The ledger reconstruction sees all 4 cycle markers. Cycle 4 hit `cycle_num >= max_cycles` → DISPATCH_ARBITER. The arbiter dispatched but the agent returned a single ruling instead of an array.

### Downstream impact

- Story c4f1-c18d-0000-4001 (SC10 evidence): closure requires demonstrating DEFER AND DROP rulings. With the fallback path the only ruling type emitted is BLOCK. Story cannot close until this is fixed.
- Epic b575-ac1c-f720-4839 (SC10): same blocker; epic cannot close while c4f1 is open.
- Arbiter PR #270 marker is posted but the per-finding rulings are all safety-fallback BLOCKs, not the agent's genuine rulings.

### Suspected root cause (not investigated yet — for the investigator sub-agent)

The `code-reviewer-arbiter` agent (`plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-arbiter.md`) may have a prompt issue that causes the agent to return one consolidated ruling instead of one-per-finding. Other possibilities: (a) token budget truncating the JSON array, (b) findings serialized in a way that conflates entries, (c) schema_version mismatch (agent emits 1.0.0 ruling but the array contract changed). The fixture-replay test (`tests/scripts/test-cycle-arbiter.sh` per epic b575 SC9) passes — the broken behavior is specific to the LIVE LLM dispatch path, not the fixture replay path.

### Acceptance criteria

- The arbiter agent MUST return one ruling per input finding (array length = findings length) for the dispatched live path.
- A regression test MUST exercise the LIVE dispatch path (or a faithful mock of it) and assert array length parity, not just fixture replay.
- After the fix, running 4 cycles on a synthetic scenario with diverse findings MUST produce BOTH BLOCK and DEFER and DROP rulings (the epic b575 SC10 evidence requirement).
data.title: [arbiter]: cycle-end arbiter returns 1 ruling for N findings on live PR -> safety fallback all-BLOCK; DEFER/DROP unreachable
